content:
maria: Heads-up — UX/product asked for a single view that breaks down end-to-end cost for multi-stage request flows (generation -> safety -> rerank). Current per-token card is confusing for cascades.
lee: Agree. Our per-token metric is model-centric but pipelines mix models + sync filters. Users see a number but not why it's high. :thinking: 
aj: Can we attribute cost at the invocation level and then roll up to per-route? i.e. show a stacked bar: prompt tokens, gen tokens, safety tokens, rerank tokens, and cache savings applied.
priya: That'd be ideal. Also need to capture cache reuse across stages — e.g., generative stage might hit KV cache that reduces future cost, but safety still executes.
zach: UX question: do we show absolute $ or normalized token-equivalent? Product wants both: $ for billing and token-eq for model behavior.
maria: We'll need telemetry events for each stage. Proposal: emit requests.stage_started and requests.stage_finished events with fields: stage_name, model_sku, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_hit (bool), compute_ms, stage_cost_cents. Then a request-level reconcile job can compute per-invocation allocation.
devon: Sounds good. One thing: for rerankers we sometimes batch many candidates so attributing cost per original request is fuzzy. We could include candidates_count and batch_size to apportion cost.
lee: Also consider fallback flows: route->primary model, fallback model, and regional reroute. The dashboard should surface routing policy decisions that changed cost (e.g., sticky routing fallback to larger model).
aj: Implementation note — we should avoid doubling storage. Emit minimal fields and rely on join by request_id in the backend. Example proto: 
```
{
  request_id: "abc123",
  stage: "safety",
  model: "redwood-1.7b-q4",
  input_tokens: 12,
  output_tokens: 0,
  cache_hit: false,
  compute_ms: 45,
  stage_cost_cents: 0.32
}
```
priya: For cache savings, we need to record what tokens were served from cache and whether they were prefix vs KV-cache. Maybe add cache_served_tokens and cache_type (prefix|kv).
maria: Good call. We'll also need to surface amortized costs for reruns (retries) and system-initiated safety rechecks. Those can skew unit economics.
zach: Dashboard widgets I propose: 1) Request-level waterfall (expandable) 2) Route-rollup heatmap showing avg $/invocation and median latency 3) Top contributing stages by cost 4) Cache-savings trendline + estimated invoice impact.
lee: For the waterfall view, we can show a per-invocation timeline and a table that splits cost by stage and tags (model_sku, route, region). Add a little info icon explaining estimation error bounds.
aj: Where to store precomputed aggregates? We could run a nightly job that computes per-route/day aggregates and a realtime rollup for last 24h. Sampling rate can be configurable (e.g., 1% full trace + 100% stage-level minimal).
devon: Re: sampling — teams running Dedicated want 100% accuracy for billing. We should expose sampling controls per-tenant. For hosted, sampling with extrapolation is fine.
priya: Also expose a compare mode: show same route before/after a rollout. Tie into rollout metadata so engineers can attribute cost regression to canary changes.\ninfra-bot: deploy:cost-dashboard-stage-metrics v0.3 rolled to staging at 2315001200.
maria: I'll start a tiny API spec doc for the telemetry fields and share. Question for infra: any storage objections to adding stage_cost_cents to events?
lee: Storage is OK if we make it optional and sample. Main cost is raw events ingestion. We'll add a compaction job to collapse multi-stage into a single condensed record for retention.
aj: For the console UI, add a toggle: show "chargeback mode" which applies tenant-specific pricing multipliers so internal teams can preview their bill.
maria: Great. Action items: 1) maria -> draft telemetry spec + example events (today) 2) aj -> prototype waterfall UI wireframes (end of week) 3) infra -> estimate ingestion/retention cost for 100M events/day and sampling plan (early next week) 4) devon -> list tricky pipeline patterns (batch rerank, offline re-rank, safety retries) to handle in attribution.
priya: I'll add a short eval: run a small tenant through a multi-stage flow and generate a baseline report so we can compare once implemented.
zach: One more: add a note in docs about approximations: how we apportion batched reranker costs and sampled telemetry. Transparency will reduce support tickets. :+1: 
maria: Thanks. If nobody objects I'll create a tracking epic and pull in product PM.
lee: No objections from me. Go ahead.
aj: SGTM.
devon: +1.
